findings.summary: The doc names an agent skill's `SKILL.md` as a body of writing the unmodeled report surfaces, but `unmodeled_markdown` filters it out because the stem `skill` is in `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS`.
findings.evidence: doc (coverage.md:64): "two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references) … Naming the groups keeps the number honest"  ||  code (coverage.py:53-55): `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS = {..., "skill", ...}` and (coverage.py:123-124) `if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(md))[0].lower() in CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS: continue  # README/CHANGELOG/… are docs, not an unmodeled corpus`. A `skills/` tree of three `SKILL.md` files therefore yields `unmodeled == []`, never mentioning the corpus the doc says is reported.
findings.suggestion: Either drop `"skill"` from `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS` for the unmodeled pass (keeping it only for the orphan pass), or amend coverage.md §Unmodeled to say that `SKILL.md` itself is filtered as a conventional doc name and only its reference files count toward a group.

verification.doc_quote: **Why:** two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references).
verification.why: The cited line (L64) is the section's "**Why:**" rationale explaining the motivation for the feature, not a normative claim about which files the report emits; the normative rule on L63 ("is not a conventional doc name") and AC-4 (`skills/*/reference.md`) match the code.

findings.summary: The Definitions table defines UNMODELED by "no code sibling", while the code excludes any markdown whose whole directory contains candidate code.
findings.evidence: doc (coverage.md:22): "UNMODELED | A directory tree of at least 3 markdown files that same-stem pairing cannot reach — no code sibling, not a conventional doc."  ||  code (coverage.py:115-120): `code_dirs = {os.path.dirname(rel) for rel in candidate}` … `if d in code_dirs: continue`. So `notes/a.md` in a directory that also holds `notes/b.py` has no code sibling yet is never unmodeled — §3 (L63) states the real rule ("sits in a directory holding no candidate code").
findings.suggestion: Reword the table row to match §3: "markdown in a directory that holds no candidate code file, not a conventional doc".

verification.doc_quote: | INV-8 | Every path in `unmodeled` sits in a directory holding no candidate code file, so no file is ever both unmodeled and paired. |
verification.why: The loose Definitions gloss on L22 is stated correctly elsewhere in the same doc — §3 L63 ("sits in a directory holding no candidate code") and INV-8 — which match the code exactly.
